newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to complain to WTO over Indonesia car policy.
newsitem.headline: Japan to complain to WTO over Indonesia car policy.

text.p: Japan announced Wednesday that it would complain to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) over Indonesia's national car policy, forming a united front with its traditional trade adversary, the United States.

Japan's Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said Japan planned to file a complaint with WTO over the issue within a week or so, but Tokyo ruled out using trade or aid retaliation measures as a way to settle the dispute.

"There is a strong suspicion that Indonesia's national car policy contravenes WTO rules. We are very concerned, and we have been repeatedly expressing our fears to (Indonesia's) President Suharto," government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama told reporters.
In Jakarta, Indonesian Trade and Industry Minister Tunky Ariwibowo said Indonesia was ready to argue its case.
"We are ready to face the WTO," he told reporters. "We will hire laywers."
Indonesia's national car plan, announced earlier this year, has come under fire from Japan, the United States and the European Union as a violation of world trade rules.
Indonesia said in February that a firm controlled by President Suharto's youngest son, Hutomo Mandala Putra, would get tax breaks to manufacture sedans in collaboration with South Korea's Kia Motors.

The company, PT Timor Putra Nasional, is the only firm granted this privilege. It must raise local content to 60 percent within three years of starting up but has been allowed to import an initial batch of cars duty-free from South Korea.
